name: Facet
text:
Choose a high-contrast light theme by default with a one-click toggle to dark mode. It ensures errors and muted colors are visible in all lighting conditions, addressing the core failure of dark themes. The trade-off is that some users may prefer the sleekness of dark mode in low light, but visibility of critical data outweighs aesthetic preference. This decision prioritizes reliability over style.

name: Pane
text: Pane: The risk isn’t just glare—it’s that dark mode hides errors *and* muted colors, so users miss critical data even when they *think* they’re seeing everything. The better alternative is to run a controlled A/B test where half the users start in light mode and half in dark, tracking error detection rates and readability in real work conditions—no toggles, just hard data. Settle it with metrics: if dark mode users miss 20% more errors, the default must change.

name: Lumen
text: DECISION: Default to a high-contrast light theme at first launch with a one-click toggle to dark mode, then run a controlled A/B test measuring error detection rates and user preference across lighting conditions. Owned by Facet (visualization-w1) and Pane (visualization-checker).
